# Analytic Muscle Replay Input Contract (Provisional)

## Scope and Status

Issue #12392 adds a strict, immutable decoder for a small synthetic analytic
muscle-replay input record. The decoder is an input contract only. It does not
advance activation, evaluate muscle force, integrate a plant, replay an
excitation trace, or establish an implementation/runtime identity. No native
OpenSim or other engine call is part of this feature. The calculation registry
remains empty; manual publication and release remain blocked.

The supported profile is one rotational coordinate, constant moment arms,
no contact, no constraints, and a scalar positive inertia. Coordinate identity
and units are explicit: radians, radians per second, newton-metres, kilograms
metres squared, and metres per radian. This profile is a bounded synthetic
fixture shape; it is not a full-body or cross-engine model.

## Input Record

`decode_analytic_replay_spec` in
`src/shared/python/motion_matching/analytic_muscle_replay_spec.py` accepts UTF-8
JSON for schema `synthetic-analytic-muscle-replay-input-v2` and profile
`rotational-1d-constant-moment-arm-no-contact-v1`. It returns frozen nested
dataclasses with tuple-valued collections. The exact-key contract includes the
coordinate and unit labels; clock and command-hold rule; initial position,
velocity, activation and prior raw excitation; activation time constants,
floor and update-rule label; plant inertia, external torque, contact,
constraints and integration-rule label; ordered muscle IDs and geometry/Hill
parameters; raw excitation commands and per-muscle raw rate limits; and
optional syntactic producer provenance.

The decoder accepts at most 65,536 input bytes, eight muscles and 128 command
steps. IDs must be nonempty, control-free, valid UTF-8 text of at most 128 UTF-8
bytes. Optional source revisions are syntax-checked as 40 lowercase
hexadecimal characters; they are not resolved, trusted, or treated as source
pins. Duplicate JSON keys, unknown or missing fields, booleans in numeric
fields, non-finite numbers, invalid units/enums, malformed shapes, duplicate
muscle IDs, and out-of-domain values fail closed.

## Clock, Geometry, and Raw Commands

Command timestamps follow the declared left-endpoint zero-order-hold grid
$t_k=t_0+k\Delta t$. The decoder requires finite, strictly increasing,
representable command times; each serialized timestamp must match its expected
grid point within an absolute tolerance of
$\min(10^{-12},\Delta t\,10^{-6})$ seconds. Relative tolerance is zero. The
finite terminal time $t_0+N\Delta t$ must advance beyond both the last expected
grid point and the last serialized command time.

The constant-moment-arm geometry check computes the initial musculotendon
length as

$$
L_{MT}(q_0)=L_{MT,ref}-r(q_0-q_{ref}),
$$

where $r$ is the declared moment arm in metres per radian. This derived value
must be finite and positive. This is a narrow contract consistency check, not a
muscle-path evaluator.

Excitation samples and the previous applied raw excitation remain raw values
in $[0,1]$. For each muscle, the first command is checked against the prior
raw value and later commands against the preceding raw value, using the exact
inclusive clipped rate interval

$$
u_k\in\left[\max(0,u_{k-1}-\dot u_{max}\Delta t),\;
                 \min(1,u_{k-1}+\dot u_{max}\Delta t)\right].
$$

The activation floor is retained separately from these raw commands. The
decoder does not compute an effective clipped command or an activation update.

## Validation and Limits

The focused tests cover exact key and shape validation, bounded UTF-8 IDs,
clock-grid and terminal checks, exact slew boundaries, state/rate bounds,
raw-zero retention with a separate activation floor, finite positive derived
geometry, frozen output, and a fresh-process import boundary. The decoder
module itself uses only the Python standard library; the subprocess test
imports and decodes a valid fixture while checking for forbidden NumPy, Qt,
biomechanics, controller and native-module components.

The validation run for this change passed 32 focused tests with one existing
DeprecationWarning, Ruff check and format, and canonical diff-scoped mypy for
the decoder file. The canonical mypy invocation was
`python -B Repository_Management/shared_scripts/run_mypy_diff.py src/shared/python/motion_matching/analytic_muscle_replay_spec.py`
with the checkout root on `PYTHONPATH` and `MYPYPATH`. The standard-conftest
focused pytest invocation was
`python -B -m pytest -o 'addopts=' -q tests/unit/motion_matching/test_analytic_muscle_replay_spec.py`.

A decoder pass establishes only that the JSON record satisfies this input
schema. It does not establish model identity, an execution worker, force
balance, activation behavior, optimization, trajectory quality, physical
validity, native replay, or parity with any registered engine. A later worker
must have its own source/runtime receipt and independently validated execution
contract before it can consume these inputs as evidence.
